headline: Rain and strong wind arrive for Thanksgiving. Central Kentucky may see wet snow late Thursday, and an official Wind Advisory covers the Upstate.
disclaimer: Independent amateur analysis. This is not an official forecast or warning. Follow the National Weather Service and local authorities during hazardous weather.

refresh.workflow: Update and commit forecast.json once. GitHub Actions automatically locks the prior issue in forecast-history.json. Then verify the GitHub Pages URL; every Google Sites embed reads the same file and refreshes automatically.

kentucky.name: Central Kentucky
kentucky.subtitle: Danville primary · Lexington comparison
kentucky.summary: A largely dry Wednesday afternoon gives way to a soaking rain late tonight through Thanksgiving. The upper low then brings colder air and wet flakes at times around Danville late Thursday into early Friday. Wind stays gusty Friday as showers taper, followed by a late freeze.
kentucky.currentConditions: At 6:15 AM EST, Danville airport reported 34°F, a 32°F dew point, light rain, five-mile visibility and a light east wind. Lexington reported 36°F and overcast skies at 5:54 AM. Radar showed intermittent inland bands with the main rain shield still developing.

days.label: Wednesday / Wednesday night
days.precipitation: Up to 30% early, 10% or less late morning and afternoon, then 95–100% overnight.
days.hazard: Wet roads return this evening, with reduced visibility in steadier rain overnight.
days.forecast: Early light showers ease this morning and leave a mainly dry travel window through late afternoon. Clouds may briefly break. Northeast wind 6–14 mph with gusts of 20–30 mph late. The main rain arrives about 7–11 PM and turns widespread around midnight to 2 AM, with about 0.5–0.75 inch possible by dawn. Most likely high 53°F, following-night low 42°F.

days.label: Thanksgiving / Thursday night
days.precipitation: Near 100%. Periods of rain, with wet flakes likely at times late Thursday or overnight around Danville.
days.hazard: Little or no accumulation is the leading outcome around Danville. A heavier band could leave a thin slushy coating on grass or elevated surfaces and isolated slick spots on bridges.
days.forecast: Expect a cold, wet Thanksgiving. Wet flakes are likely at times in the wraparound rain near Danville late Thursday into early Friday, most likely from about 8 PM to 5 AM. Lexington is more marginal, and earlier flakes are possible to the southwest. East wind turns southwest or west as the low passes, with late gusts around 25–35 mph and isolated gusts near 40 mph. About 1–2 inches of liquid is expected from Wednesday night into Friday morning, locally over 2 inches in a persistent band. Most likely high 46°F, following-night low 33°F.

days.label: Friday / early Saturday
days.precipitation: 90–100% early, falling to 30–40% by late afternoon and below 15% after evening.
days.hazard: Brief reduced visibility and isolated slick spots are possible early where Thursday night’s band left slush. Gusts and a late freeze are the other concerns.
days.forecast: Rain is likely early, with wet flakes still possible in heavier bands near daybreak. The chance of wet flakes drops as the precipitation lightens, with scattered rain showers tapering by about 7 PM. West wind 12–20 mph, gusting 25–35 mph. Wind chills may be in the 20s early. Winds ease heading into Saturday morning and temperatures fall back below freezing in much of the area. Most likely high 41°F, following-night low 29°F.

kentucky.bottomLine: Wednesday afternoon is the driest travel window before the main rain. Expect 1–2 inches of liquid, locally more, from Wednesday night into Friday morning. Wet flakes are likely at times near Danville late Thursday and early Friday, with little or no accumulation most likely. Friday turns drier by evening.
kentucky.confidence: High in the overnight and Thanksgiving rain. Medium in the timing and placement of the wet-snow band and lower for any accumulation.

upstate.name: Upstate South Carolina
upstate.subtitle: Clemson primary · Central/Pickens County comparison
upstate.summary: A cool northeast wedge holds today as rain and gusts strengthen. An official Wind Advisory covers Clemson and Central from noon Wednesday to 10 AM Thursday. The rain tapers around midday or early afternoon Thanksgiving. West winds pick up again after a brief lull and remain gusty Friday.
upstate.currentConditions: Clemson airport reported light rain, 45°F, a 26°F dew point and an east-northeast gust of 33 mph at 5:54 AM EST. Pickens reported 45°F, a 22°F dew point and ten-mile visibility at 6:15 AM. The early light rain preceded the developing main shield.

days.label: Wednesday / Wednesday night
days.hazard: Strong gusts can move unsecured objects, break small limbs and cause isolated outages. Expect wet roads and occasional ponding in heavier rain.
days.forecast: A few light showers are possible this morning. Rain fills in between about 11 AM and 3 PM and becomes steadier by evening as moist air rises over the cool wedge. Northeast wind 12–22 mph with gusts of 30–45 mph. Patchy fog and low visibility are possible late and overnight, especially in heavier showers. Most likely high 49°F, following-night low 45°F.

days.label: Thanksgiving / Thursday night
days.hazard: The advisory lasts through 10 AM. Reduced visibility and ponding are possible early, and gusty wind may return after the morning lull.
days.forecast: Expect rain and patchy fog early, with rain tapering through midday or early afternoon as the low lifts away. A morning lull and turn toward the west are followed by renewed gusts of 25–35 mph in the afternoon or evening. Some late warming is possible as the cool wedge breaks. Most locations can expect about 0.5–1.25 inches for the event, with isolated 1.5–2 inch totals possible if a rain band persists. Most likely high 55°F, following-night low 35°F.

days.label: Friday / early Saturday
days.hazard: Breezy through much of Friday with a localized freeze possible late Friday night. The issued Wind Advisory ends Thursday morning.
days.forecast: Partly sunny and dry. West-southwest wind 12–18 mph with gusts of 25–35 mph. Winds ease Friday night and sheltered spots could reach freezing by early Saturday. Exposed locations may stay a few degrees warmer where wind holds up. Most likely high 50°F, following-night low 33°F.

upstate.bottomLine: The windiest period runs Wednesday afternoon into early Thanksgiving. Rain is most widespread Wednesday night and early Thursday. Around 0.5–1.25 inches are expected across most of the corridor, with isolated 1.5–2 inches possible under a persistent band. Friday is dry and breezy.
upstate.confidence: High in Wednesday rain and gusty wind. Medium in the onset of sustained rain, the local maximum and Thursday’s wind shift. High in Friday’s drying.

sourceNotes: Chris Bailey’s November 25 analysis and snow-threat graphic place Danville in the likely-flakes area and emphasize heavier snow west and southwest. His graphic provides no local accumulation total.

The Louisville area discussion places the colder core farther south while its Danville point forecast includes a late Thursday and early Friday mix. KLEX BUFKIT wet-bulb temperatures around 2–3°C during precipitation favor melting. The independent forecast carries flakes with little or no accumulation most likely and a conditional thin grassy coating.

The official point-alert check found no active Danville alert. The Upstate alert returned the same issuance for Clemson and Central with northeast winds 10–20 mph and gusts up to 40–45 mph from noon Wednesday through 10 AM Thursday. The Friday card describes the same issuance snapshot and its prior expiry.

Upstate official point data and current model guidance support a midday to early-afternoon Thanksgiving rain taper and lower corridor totals than the prior issue. Deterministic accumulation guidance clustered around 0.3–0.9 inch, with local profiles and broader ensembles allowing more. Recast’s wetter 06Z WOOF-NAM outcome is a low-confidence upper-end check.
The WPC short-range outlook places the Slight Risk of excessive rain nearer the coast. Local NWS guidance assesses the Upstate flash-flood risk as low, with a heavier narrow band possible.

Generated November 25 in the workspace, fresh BUFKIT profiles include GFS/RRFS 06Z and HRRR/RAP 09Z for KLEX, KSME, KGSP and KAND. Nearby stations inform adjustment and timing while KDVK/KLEX and KCEU/KLQK remain the verification stations.
NOAA retired the operational NAM and nests. RRFS and REFS replace that guidance. The NAM-labeled COD chart used here is the separate Recast WOOF-NAM, initialized by GFS.

College of DuPage point products, GOES and radar were checked alongside GEFS, ECENS, GEPS, AIGEFS and AIFS member spread. The raw Danville GRIB refresh had no validated output at the source cutoff and was excluded.
At 6:25–6:26 AM EST radar and infrared showed patchy inland echoes and a developing coastal shield. Airport reports independently confirmed early light rain at Danville and Clemson.
The current accuracy summary was used for station overnight corrections, empirical range widths and the regime-specific forecast review. Tempest was excluded from Upstate analysis and verification.
Daily low temperatures refer to the following night. The third cards cover through the early Saturday 72-hour endpoint.
